niche.diet: ectoparasites, dead epidermis, mucus, carcass particles (corona), zooplankton, cuarteta juveniles

body: 32 cm length, 420 g mass; laterally compressed eel with smooth, scaleless dermis and yellow-green filtered eyes

chains.trait: Ampullary pits detect parasite nerve impulses
links: Turbid shallows block vision (<10 m visibility)
Pressure and touch sense dominate in murky water
Ectoparasites thrive in humid, high-O₂ air/water (F29)

skill.effect: The creature scans nearby clients to locate hidden parasites, then carefully extracts them, leaving the host feeling refreshed and healthy.

chains.weakness: Sudden pressure spikes from lightning or boat wakes disrupt its electroreception.
observe: Pits along the snout pulse when a fish approaches
Parasites lift off and float away as it moves
Retreats to lava crevices when thunder rolls

journal.en: It eats what the giants ignore. A living sponge for the shallows.

plausibility.summary: Reframe pits as client-finders and ambush-avoidance in turbidity (sense large visitor bioelectric field + pressure), then remove parasites by contact/taste on mucosa; optional highly speculative micro-sense only after the cleaner is already on the host. Pressure/lightning disruption stays as sensitivity to sudden hydrodynamic and EM noise, not literal ‘nerve impulse GPS’.
fixes: Reframe pits as client-finders and ambush-avoidance in turbidity (sense large visitor bioelectric field + pressure), then remove parasites by contact/taste on mucosa; optional highly speculative micro-sense only after the cleaner is already on the host. Pressure/lightning disruption stays as sensitivity to sudden hydrodynamic and EM noise, not literal ‘nerve impulse GPS’.

analogues.organism: Elasmobranch ampullae of Lorenzini (e.g. nurse shark) detect prey bioelectric fields; gymnotiform and mormyrid fish use tuberous electroreceptors for prey and social context in murky water—not for pinpointing individual copepod-scale parasites on a host.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Mucosal tongue scrapes dead epidermis and mucus
links: Shallow currents carry drifting carcass fragments and detritus
Filter feeders like Corona concentrate particulate matter
High ambient O₂ (D10) supports fast tissue turnover in hosts

skill.effect: The creature scrapes away loose mucus and dead skin from the host, feeding on the debris while clearing away the parasites that hide within.

chains.weakness: Cannot digest fibrous plant matter; starves if confined to grassy shallows.
observe: Tongue flicks in a rhythmic, tongue-like motion
Host fish stand still and relax during cleaning
Exits the water briefly when the tide drops

journal.en: A tongue built for polishing, not hunting. Mutualism pays better than predation here.

plausibility.summary: Marine cleaning mutualism is selection-favoured where parasite load is high and clients tolerate approach; mucus and epidermal nibbling match documented cleaner diets. D10/F5 high pO₂ supports host wound turnover and aerobic metabolism for a small active swimmer. Shallows detritus and Corona-style particles supply fallback calories. Opportunistic juvenile cuarteta predation weakens ‘pure mutualist’ branding but is ecologically common.
fixes: Marine cleaning mutualism is selection-favoured where parasite load is high and clients tolerate approach; mucus and epidermal nibbling match documented cleaner diets. D10/F5 high pO₂ supports host wound turnover and aerobic metabolism for a small active swimmer. Shallows detritus and Corona-style particles supply fallback calories. Opportunistic juvenile cuarteta predation weakens ‘pure mutualist’ branding but is ecologically common.

analogues.organism: Bluestreak cleaner wrasse (Labroides dimidiatus) and Indo-Pacific cleaner shrimp (Lysmata amboinensis)—ectoparasite removal plus mucus/tissue feeding; cleaners also cheat with biting juveniles.

chains.trait: Laterally compressed eel body for undulatory propulsion
links: High drag in shallow waters due to sediment and plankton bloom (F20)
Terminal velocity is lower than on Earth (F4, D16)
Limbless form reduces frontal area in dense medium (D11)

skill.effect: It glides through cloudy water with barely a ripple, making it very hard to spot when swimming nearby.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to sudden turbulence; loses maneuverability in heavy rain or storm surges (F8).
observe: Tails flick to stir sand when alarmed

journal.en: No limbs, just a wave. The heavy water demands a dancer, not a runner.

plausibility.summary: Anguilliform swimming in viscous, sediment-rich nearshore water minimizes bow wave and suits stealth beside clients; limb loss from a shallow benthic larval lineage is a standard island-radiation (F27) reduction. Mass ~420 g at 32 cm is consistent with a deep-bodied laterally compressed fish, not a ribbon eel. D11/F4 higher drag favours low-profile swimmers over sprint cruisers.
fixes: Anguilliform swimming in viscous, sediment-rich nearshore water minimizes bow wave and suits stealth beside clients; limb loss from a shallow benthic larval lineage is a standard island-radiation (F27) reduction. Mass ~420 g at 32 cm is consistent with a deep-bodied laterally compressed fish, not a ribbon eel. D11/F4 higher drag favours low-profile swimmers over sprint cruisers.

analogues.organism: Snake eels and sand-dwelling ophichthids (anguilliform, cryptic in turbid littoral zones); paedomorphic limb reduction as in many elongate teleosts.

chains.trait: Diurnal activity cycle synchronized with high tide
links: Parasite feeding is most efficient under scattered daylight (F1, F23)
Low tide exposes shallows to UV spike and heat (F14, F20)
High tide brings nutrient-rich upwelling and extends foraging range (F13)

skill.effect: It rides the sweeping tides into friendly waters, visibly earning the steady favor of Brújula and Cuarteta.

chains.weakness: Cannot survive prolonged exposure during extreme low tides; must seek splash pools or lava tubes (F9).
observe: Active only when waves cover the shallows
Forms loose lines along known cleaning rocks
Dives into dark crevices as the sun sets

journal.en: It lives by the moon's pull. When the water retreats, it hides; when the water returns, it works.

plausibility.summary: Make activity ‘inundation-gated’ first: work whenever shallows are deep enough, prefer daylight when tide and sun align (+rapport window); crepuscular or brief nocturnal high-tide cleans allowed. Low tide → splash pools/lava crevices (already in lore) without requiring impossible diurnal-only scheduling.

analogues.organism: Intertidal and shallow reef fishes that concentrate feeding on flooded reefs (many labrids and gobies); cleaner wrasse activity peaks by light and client presence rather than a single rigid tide×day gate.

relations.note: Eats juveniles and drifting plankton aggregates near Cuarteta foraging grounds.
Adult Brújula occasionally snaps up the cleaner in turbid shallows.

changelog.what: removed rejected references and non-existent root facts (roots recovered from the derivation items cited in the links, else F27)

body_plan.origin: derived from shallow-dwelling larval stages that lost limbs for undulatory propulsion in dense, viscous water

temperament: placid mutualist, easily startled by pressure spikes
secrets: Parasite cache: find a cluster of cleaned parasites lodged in a lava crevice after a storm.
Client trust: watch a Brújula stand perfectly still while the cleaner works its gills, then nudge it to gain +10 rapport.
moments: High tide, the creature lines up with a wounded Espinodo or Coloso at the shore, offering to clean a deep abrasion; the giant lowers its head, trusting it.

journal.en: A tongue built for polishing, not hunting. Mutualism pays better than predation here.
It lives by the moon's pull. When the water retreats, it hides; when the water returns, it works.
